Emma — thanks for the plan, that helps. Drafting a concise primer below and attaching a short proposal PDF. High level we support both marginal and blended billing; the main tradeoffs are predictability vs visibility into marginal savings when you cross breakpoints.

Attachment: Redwood-Proposal-v1.pdf

Short primer (for the 3-tier example you asked about):
- Marginal: each breakpoint reduces the incremental token price for tokens above that breakpoint. Effective $/1k is derived by summing per-band cost. Flexible and aligns incentives to grow, slightly more variable month-to-month.
- Blended: one single effective rate applied to all usage in the period based on which band total usage falls into. Simpler invoicing; downside is the step change (you may get a large one-time drop when crossing band).

Proposal summary (high level):
- Commit: 5M tokens/month baseline, with 3 breakpoints at 10M and 25M tokens.
- Prices (example): base $35/1k, tier1 $28/1k (10M-25M), tier2 $20/1k (25M+).
- Billing: we prefer marginal by default. Blended available if HealthLytics needs simpler accounting.
- Minimum guarantee fence suggestion: a two-part mechanism:
   1) Minimum guarantee floor (MGF): you commit to a monthly minimum spend (eg $X/month) that counts toward the commit.
   2) Minority fence: if actual usage is between 80% and 95% of committed monthly tokens, we apply a reduced true-up: only 50% of shortfall billed as true-up (so limited clawback). Below 80% full shortfall applies.

Why this structure? It reduces the cash shock of small misses while preserving economics for larger shortfalls. It also keeps the incentive to grow.

Next steps: I’ll run concrete marginal vs blended numbers against your spreadsheet and Marissa/Ben will sanity-check the finance treatment. Is monthly true-up acceptable for you?

Looping you two in with the ask for numeric examples. I ran quick math against HealthLytics' sheet — raw bullets below, keep these internal.

Internal summary (3-tier example, commit = 5M tokens/month):
- Pricing bands (example):
   * Band A (0-10M): $35/1k (base)
   * Band B (10M-25M): $28/1k
   * Band C (25M+): $20/1k

Scenario A: Month where HealthLytics hits 85% of 5M commit (4.25M tokens)
- Marginal billing: all tokens billed at per-band marginal rates given actual usage; effective rate computes to ~$35/1k (no band crossing, so same as base).
- True-up under proposed minority fence: shortfall = 0.75M tokens -> standard true-up would bill the entire shortfall at base price (~$26,250). Under minority fence (50% mitigation) they pay 0.375M * $35/1k = $13,125. So reduced cash impact.

Scenario B: Month where HealthLytics hits 94% of 5M commit (4.7M tokens)
- Shortfall = 0.3M tokens -> full true-up would be 0.3M * $35/1k = $10,500. With minority fence at 50% they'd pay $5,250.

Notes on blended vs marginal effect for near-miss months:
- If they were to cross a breakpoint in the month, marginal helps them capture the lower incremental bands immediately. Blended could create a single-step change that looks nicer in accounting but could swing invoice materially when a band is crossed.

Marissa recommendation: offer marginal billing default with a hybrid option: blended smoothing (quarterly smoothing) for customers who need that level of accounting symmetry. For the contract, propose the minority fence language as Markus suggested and add a cap: clawback exposure per rolling quarter <= 1.5x monthly committed spend.

Agree with Marissa. A few finance-side clarifications for the proposal PDF:
- Invoice cadence: monthly true-up is fine, but we need to include net-30 payment terms and explicit description of how true-up is calculated and when credits apply.
- Minority fence mechanics: recommend writing the clause as: "For months where actual usage >= 80% and <95% of committed tokens, Customer pays 50% of the monetary shortfall (calculated at the base band rate)."
- Clawback cap: we can accept the rolling-quarter cap at 1.5x of one month’s committed spend, provided we include a materiality carve-out for usage anomalies due to third-party outages or Force Majeure.

I ran the numbers and attached a simple CSV with the model output (assumes 5M commit, the band prices above). Attachment: financial-model-breakdown.csv

Example line items from the model (monthly):
- Commit: 5,000,000 tokens -> committed spend @ base = $175,000/month
- If actual = 4,250,000 (85%): true-up at 50% -> $13,125 (as Marissa calculated) -> invoice = base billed usage + true-up adjustments and any similar credits.

We also need to be explicit on credits vs pre-paid offsets (ie whether unused commit converts to credits applied to future invoices). My recommendation: unused committed dollars can be rolled forward as credits up to one quarter. Beyond that, we do not carry forward credits unless agreed in an addendum.
